data.title: Session
data.tagline: State a service keeps for a signed-in person and can look up using a browser-held identifier
data.learningOutcome: When a page asks you to sign in again, you can tell whether the session expired, the cookie was cleared, or authentication itself failed.
data.description: After sign-in, a request that matches the cookie domain, path, and browser policies can carry a session identifier, which the service uses to find a still-valid session. A session may expire or be revoked, prompting another sign-in; this differs from the current password check failing.

learning.assumes: You have used sites that require sign-in, or been asked to sign in again.
learning.outcome: When a page asks you to sign in again, you can tell whether the session expired, the cookie was cleared, or authentication itself failed.

distinctions.label: Cookie
distinctions.explanation: A cookie is the technical carrier of the identifier; a session is the state kept server-side. They work together but are not the same thing.

distinctions.label: Token
distinctions.explanation: A token is a credential the client holds and presents; a session keeps state on the server and matches the identifier each time.

explanation.title: The server creates a session at sign-in
explanation.text: After credentials pass, the server creates a session state for this person and gives the browser an identifier.

explanation.title: Matching requests carry the identifier
explanation.text: Requests carry it when cookie domain, path, and browser policies match; the service looks up the session to keep the user signed in.

explanation.title: It fails after expiry or clearing
explanation.text: When the session expires or the identifier is cleared, the server no longer recognizes it and the page asks for sign-in.

data.boundary: Being asked to sign in again does not mean the password is wrong: session expiry is the signed-in state ending, while authentication failure is the identity not being accepted. Separate state is gone from identity is wrong first.

lessonPractice.title: A user reports being asked to sign in again every half hour. What is the most likely cause?

options.label: The session lifetime is too short, so the identifier stops being accepted
options.feedback: Correct. A short lifetime makes users re-sign-in frequently; adjusting the lifetime or supporting remember-me helps.

options.label: The user mistyped the password, so authentication fails each time
options.feedback: Being able to sign in proves the password is right; the issue is that the signed-in state does not persist.

options.label: The database is down, so all operations fail
options.feedback: A database outage causes broader failures, not just periodic re-sign-in prompts.

data.agentPrompt: Users are asked to sign in again every half hour. Check the session lifetime setting and state its current value; if it is too short, adjust it to a reasonable duration and confirm an hour of continuous use stays signed in.
